rStL7niR7gs.summary: CGP Grey's animated adaptation of The Dictator's Handbook, explaining how rulers stay in power by keeping a small group of key supporters happy rather than ruling fairly. It lays out selectorate theory and how resources shape regimes.
rStL7niR7gs.why: HN treats it as the standard short summary of how power and political incentives work, applied to governments, companies and workplaces.

r-TLSBdHe1A.summary: Emery Berger explains why performance is hard to measure and deliver on modern hardware, showing how code layout and alignment can swamp optimization effects. He presents Stabilizer for statistically sound evaluation and Coz, a causal profiler.
r-TLSBdHe1A.why: It is the standard recommendation for anyone puzzled by unexplained benchmark changes from tiny code edits, and for learning about causal profiling.

rX0ItVEVjHc.summary: Mike Acton of Insomniac Games argues that a program's purpose is transforming data, and shows how common C++ approaches work against that in performance-critical game development. He covers cache behavior, data layout and the limits of compilers.
rX0ItVEVjHc.why: It is the go-to talk HN points to for data-oriented design and hardware-aware performance thinking, despite Acton's blunt style.

rNu8XDBSn10.summary: CGP Grey's quick, witty explainer on the differences between the United Kingdom, Great Britain and England, and the countries that make up the UK.
rNu8XDBSn10.why: HN recommends it as the standard short answer whenever someone confuses Britain, the UK and England.

r3snVCRo_bI.summary: Folding Ideas uses the rise and fall of the YouTube competitor VidMe to examine why platforms are not friends to creators. It argues that alternatives to big platforms tend to attract the users banned from the original and lack a core vision.
r3snVCRo_bI.why: HN commenters cite it whenever a thread asks why clones of or alternatives to YouTube, Reddit or Twitter fail or turn toxic.

rOwMW6agpTI.summary: Bruce Dang of Microsoft gives a 27C3 talk on how the Stuxnet vulnerabilities were found and analyzed. He walks through the techniques used to triage them and the details of each zero-day exploit, down to the opcode level.
rOwMW6agpTI.why: HN recommends it as the definitive technical deep dive into Stuxnet's zero-days from someone who analyzed it first-hand.

roBkg-iPrbw.summary: Ahoy's documentary traces tracker music from early Amiga software like SoundMonitor and Soundtracker through the demoscene, Protracker, and PC trackers such as Screamtracker and FastTracker. It covers the sound, culture and history of 16-bit module music.
roBkg-iPrbw.why: It is the go-to chronological, in-depth overview of tracker music, recommended whenever trackers, the Amiga or the demoscene come up.

r-A78RgMhZU.summary: David Beazley's PyCon India closing keynote, in which he live-codes a stack machine and grows it into an interpreter that runs WebAssembly, then uses it to play a Rust-written game. It requires no prior WebAssembly knowledge.
r-A78RgMhZU.why: Regarded as a brilliant live-coding talk that teaches WASM and interpreter writing, with several calling it among the best conference talks they have seen.

rI8tNMsozo0.summary: Rich Hickey's keynote at RailsConf 2012, a close sibling of his 'Simple Made Easy' talk. He distinguishes simple (not intertwined) from easy (familiar), and argues that software complexity comes from complecting things, with Rails-specific examples including large gem collections.
rI8tNMsozo0.why: HN recommends it as an alternative or companion to 'Simple Made Easy', and quotes its ideas about simplicity, complexity and 'hairballs' in discussions of frameworks, JSON and data design.

ras_VYgA77Q.summary: A DEF CON 26 talk by investigative journalists and hackers on the fake science industry, with bogus conferences and predatory journals that give studies false credibility. It draws on a large investigation into the money behind them.
ras_VYgA77Q.why: Recommended as a funny but depressing investigation, and the usual link in threads on predatory publishing and fake citations.

rHIkrotSwcc.summary: Chandler Carruth argues in a CppCon 2019 talk that C++ has no truly zero-cost abstractions. Using examples like unique_ptr, ABI constraints and compile-time costs, he shows that abstractions cost runtime, compile time or human effort.
rHIkrotSwcc.why: HN commenters cite it whenever zero-cost abstraction claims come up, especially for why unique_ptr is not free on some ABIs.

rRbY3TMUcgQ.summary: A humorous 10-minute parody sequel to Erlang: The Movie, in which Erlang's creators discuss the aging language and meet a surprise helper. It plays on the Outlaw Techno Psychobitch joke for OTP.
rRbY3TMUcgQ.why: HN loves it as a funny, shorter sequel and even uses it to introduce Erlang in university classes.

rFejpH_tAHM.summary: Rob Pike's dotGo 2015 talk argues that Go only seems simple, and that its simplicity hides real complexity that is part of the design. He explains the thinking behind Go's restraint in features.
rFejpH_tAHM.why: HN returns to it to explain why Go deliberately resists syntactic sugar and new features.

rOzrJjdZDRQ.summary: A HOPE X talk giving an in-depth explanation of how elevators work, from their history in hacker culture to using their control systems to bypass building security. It covers features and abilities of elevators that most people never see.
rOzrJjdZDRQ.why: HN commenters call it one of the most entertaining and informative con talks, and a good window into elevators from a hacker's view.

rE3j_RHkqJc.summary: CGP Grey explains how ideas spread like germs, and why content that triggers outrage spreads fastest, using a study on what makes online content viral. He argues that opposing outrage-driven memes feed each other.
rE3j_RHkqJc.why: HN links it constantly in threads on social media, polarization and outrage as the canonical explanation of why angry content wins.

rhgwIhB58PA.summary: Veritasium debunks the idea of learning styles, such as being a visual learner, with an interview with Daniel Willingham and a memory experiment. It argues that a multimodal approach helps everyone.
rhgwIhB58PA.why: The standard link whenever someone claims to be a visual learner or learning styles come up, with sources listed in the description.

rQmqVVmMB3k.summary: A What I've Learned video arguing that industrial seed and vegetable oils have displaced saturated fats and harmed health. It covers the history of vegetable oils, the American Heart Association's role, and rising consumption.
rQmqVVmMB3k.why: HN commenters recommend it as an accessible summary of the case against seed oils, and some say it changed what fats they cook with.

re96UgMk6GQ.summary: Simon Peyton Jones gives Churchill College's annual computer science lecture on Haskell's birth and evolution. He covers the most influential ideas, from laziness to monads and type system evolution, plus current developments and guesses about the future.
re96UgMk6GQ.why: Recommended as a funny, accessible history of Haskell that is valuable even for people interested in language design in general.

rnmcRTnTNC8.summary: Deviant Ollam, head of a physical penetration testing team, presents tactics for getting into buildings, from bypassing door levers with a wire to defeating bank doors. He argues that physical security is often surprisingly weak.
rnmcRTnTNC8.why: HN recommends it as an entertaining overview of physical pen testing, and cites it when threads discuss how easily doors and locks are bypassed.

rvkEpstd9os.summary: An Al Jazeera investigation into Boeing's 787 Dreamliner, featuring current and former engineers who voice safety concerns. It covers quality control problems at the South Carolina plant and the roots of the battery problems that grounded the plane.
rvkEpstd9os.why: Boeing threads cite it as early evidence of deep cultural and quality problems at Boeing, years before the 737 MAX crashes.

rvskMHn0sqQ.summary: Kurzgesagt makes a selfish case for improving the world, arguing that helping people far away raises prosperity and innovation for everyone, including yourself. The animated video frames this as egoistic altruism and positive-sum cooperation.
rvskMHn0sqQ.why: HN commenters link it to argue for cooperation and engagement over isolation, and as an accessible statement of positive-sum thinking.

r6sGWTCMz2k.summary: 3Blue1Brown introduces Fourier series, from the heat equation to drawing arbitrary shapes with rotating circles. It builds a visual intuition for decomposing functions into sine waves.
r6sGWTCMz2k.why: Recommended as the visual explanation that makes Fourier series and transforms click, even for laypeople.

r9eQth4Q5jg.summary: Casey Muratori gives a fast tour of the RemedyBG debugger for Windows, which he uses daily. He shows its speed and features, especially the watch window.
r9eQth4Q5jg.why: HN points to it as a demonstration of what fast, well-built developer tooling looks like and of why a debugger beats print statements.

rgaTLrZGlk0.summary: Andrew Huang teaches the basics of music theory in about half an hour, covering intervals, chords and patterns. He stresses understanding how music works over memorizing terminology.
rgaTLrZGlk0.why: HN recommends it as a concise, approachable starting point for anyone asking how to learn music theory.

rxOKEsBx4NU.summary: Ross Scott's Game Dungeon episode on Deus Ex, a long review of the game covering its narrative, politics and economic philosophy as well as its design.
rxOKEsBx4NU.why: HN recommends it as a deeper look at Deus Ex's themes, and as the best essay on its politics and economics.

rzQEIRRJ2T0.summary: A three-minute Emacs Rocks screencast demonstrating Magit, the Git interface inside Emacs, including staging and other everyday operations.
rzQEIRRJ2T0.why: HN users share it as the quick demo that shows what Magit can do, for people unfamiliar with it.

r8RxkpUvxK0.summary: Moishe Lettvin, a former Google engineer, shares lessons from 250 interviews and his time on the hiring committee. He tells how the committee given anonymized packets, including its own, would hire almost none of them.
r8RxkpUvxK0.why: Linked often in hiring-process threads for the anecdote about Google's committee refusing to hire itself, as evidence interviews are noisy.

rDPj5zI66LA.summary: Isaac Arthur surveys the popular proposed solutions to the Fermi Paradox in a 71-minute compendium. He weighs the strengths and weaknesses of each argument.
rDPj5zI66LA.why: HN commenters recommend Arthur's Fermi Paradox videos as a thorough, clear treatment of the subject.

rJjKP8vYjpQ.summary: A short clip from the film The Gambler in which John Goodman's character gives a monologue about the 'position of fuck you': building enough financial security that you owe nobody anything. The scene is a compact statement of financial independence as freedom.
rJjKP8vYjpQ.why: HN points to it as the source and best distillation of 'fuck you money', in threads about FIRE, windfalls, layoffs and financial literacy.

rRi8LptvFZY.summary: Velcro Brand's legal team makes a short, humorous ad asking people not to use "velcro" as a noun or verb and to say hook and loop instead. It is a tongue-in-cheek lesson in defending a trademark against genericization.
rRi8LptvFZY.why: HN cites it as the go-to example of a company defending its trademark, and many also find it funny.

rn7MmS3vazU.summary: Pink Floyd's Echoes played in sync with the final Jupiter and Beyond the Infinite segment of Kubrick's 2001: A Space Odyssey. The song's length closely matches the sequence.
rn7MmS3vazU.why: HN commenters share it as a favorite audiovisual experience, with some calling the sync the best thing they have seen.

r0plv_nIzsQ.summary: Looking Glass Universe explains de Broglie-Bohm pilot wave theory (Bohmian mechanics) as an alternative to the standard interpretation of quantum mechanics. The video lays out the pros and cons of the theory and links to related videos on contextuality and entanglement.
r0plv_nIzsQ.why: HN commenters recommend the channel as a clear, well-made source on quantum mechanics and common misconceptions about Bohmian mechanics.

r2CbbBLVaPk.summary: A short talk by Will Dayble of Squareweave arguing that you should design software as if the user were drunk: distracted, impaired in attention and vision, and prone to misreading. It is a user experience talk built around that framing.
r2CbbBLVaPk.why: HN users recommend it as a memorable, short way to build empathy for users' confusing mistakes and to design for distraction.

r6Rp-uo6HmI.summary: Tom Scott explains why confetti and snow wreck video quality, using interframe compression and bitrate. He demonstrates it live by changing the quality on screen.
r6Rp-uo6HmI.why: Used as the clearest short demonstration of why noisy, high-motion content is hard for video compression.

rCMh7srOqvw.summary: A short first episode in Zaiste's Doom Emacs series, showing how to get started with Doom, an Emacs configuration aimed at Vim users. It presents Doom as a polished, fast, batteries-included distribution.
rCMh7srOqvw.why: HN users recommend the series to newcomers learning Emacs, Doom, org-mode, projectile and magit.

rEf35NtlBLg.summary: Cockpit footage of a Swiss Airbus A340 crew dealing with rising oil temperature in one engine on a Zurich to Shanghai flight, ending with a safety landing. It shows the pilots' procedures through the emergency.
rEf35NtlBLg.why: Recommended as a captivating look at how a professional crew calmly handles an in-flight engine problem.

rFqL9CkNxXw.summary: Astrophysicist David Kipping presents the halo drive, a proposed way to propel a starship to a good fraction of light speed by gaining energy from a black hole. The video is based on his peer-reviewed paper and explains why energy is the main obstacle to interstellar flight.
rFqL9CkNxXw.why: HN readers point to it as a clear explanation of a theoretical fuel-free propulsion concept from a channel they respect.

rbu7Zu5X1zI.summary: Grant Sanderson of 3Blue1Brown shows his workflow for animating math videos with Manim, with Ben Sparks. He codes scenes live, including a Lorenz attractor, and walks through example scenes.
rbu7Zu5X1zI.why: Recommended as a rare detailed look at how 3b1b videos are made, including live debugging of his rendering engine.

rimtaSgGz_4.summary: Cory Doctorow's DEF CON 31 talk describes how platforms decay in a pattern he calls enshittification. He lays out a plan to stop it through antitrust, interoperability and fixing the law.
rimtaSgGz_4.why: Recommended in threads on big tech, monopolies and adversarial interoperability as the clearest statement of his argument.

rk6z1vP4Eo8.summary: Robert Bussard's 2006 Google Tech Talk on inertial electrostatic confinement fusion, a compact approach he argued could be cheap and clean, using boron-hydrogen fuel without neutron radiation. It runs about 93 minutes and covers the physics, funding history and his proposed development path.
rk6z1vP4Eo8.why: Recommended as an intense, insightful look at Bussard's IEC fusion work, frequently cited in fusion threads for his claim that it could be developed for about $200M.

rrkrvAUbU9Y.summary: Dan Pink's TED talk argues that traditional carrot-and-stick rewards often fail for creative work, drawing on the candle problem and social science research. He points to autonomy, mastery and purpose as better motivators.
rrkrvAUbU9Y.why: HN cites it whenever money as an incentive comes up, as evidence that rewards can backfire for creative white-collar work.

rtR63-ecUNo.summary: Jerobeam Fenderson shows how to draw a mushroom on an oscilloscope in XY mode using stereo audio, then animates it by modulating with a larger wave. Pd and Max4Live patches are provided.
rtR63-ecUNo.why: HN finds it mesmerizing and uses it to build intuition for waveforms and oscilloscope XY drawing.

rv-mFSoZOkE.summary: In a 2010 Google Tech Talk, Kirk Sorensen gives an economic analysis of what spent nuclear fuel actually contains. He argues it is mostly valuable material that can be partitioned and reused, not just waste to be isolated for 100,000 years.
rv-mFSoZOkE.why: HN readers recommend it as the best explanation of what nuclear waste really is and how much of it is reusable fuel.

r1ZLGqL1FMo.summary: Paolo fromTOKYO explains why foreign tourists get arrested in Japan, covering strict laws and the justice system's very high conviction rate.
r1ZLGqL1FMo.why: Commenters mostly use it as a lead-in to recommending interviews with Japanese lawyers about detention and the justice system, and one says they learned from it.

r9rGX91rq5I.summary: CGP Grey explains how the 2015 UK general election showed the flaws of first-past-the-post voting, with parties like UKIP winning many votes but few seats.
r9rGX91rq5I.why: HN recommends it as a short, clear illustration of how first-past-the-post misrepresents voters.

rAl-9HwD858.summary: In this first Crust of Rust episode, Jon Gjengset live-codes an example that needs multiple explicit lifetime annotations. Along the way he covers string types and generics over a custom trait.
rAl-9HwD858.why: Recommended as a slow-paced, detailed live-coding session that makes lifetimes click once you are past Rust basics.

rHP-OPXK2ig.summary: Scotty Allen of Strange Parts travels through Shenzhen's Huaqiangbei markets and learns to upgrade an iPhone 6s from 16GB to 128GB by swapping its flash chip. It is part 3 of his custom iPhone series and shows the difficulty of the hands-on repair work.
rHP-OPXK2ig.why: HN people recommend it for its vivid look at Shenzhen's repair culture and for the flash chip upgrade, and cite it in discussions of hardware modding.

rURRYI66E54.summary: Rob Miles explains on Computerphile how language models generate plausible text and how transformers improved on recurrent networks, with a look at what comes next.
rURRYI66E54.why: Pointed to as an accessible early explanation of transformers and attention for newcomers.

ra_9zU-mnl8.summary: Zack Freedman introduces Gridfinity, his free, open-source modular workshop storage system of 3D-printable bins and baseplates. The video walks through the design, the parametric templates and the many module types that fit parts, tools and accessories.
ra_9zU-mnl8.why: HN points people to it as the original explanation of what Gridfinity is and why it exists, in threads about the project and its catalogs.

rgGmKD87U3M.summary: A 1990 Lotus sales demo of Improv, a spreadsheet built for the NeXT computer that rethought the grid with named categories and multiple views. The uploader, who tested it at Price Waterhouse, presents it as an early, innovative vision of the spreadsheet.
rgGmKD87U3M.why: HN links it in spreadsheet-reinvention threads as the clearest look at what Improv did differently, with a distinctive NeXTstep aesthetic.

rmueBVrLKcY.summary: Joe Armstrong's GOTO 2018 talk contrasts the problems computer scientists study with the problems users have. He revisits forgotten great ideas such as tuple spaces, flow-based programming, Xanadu and Unix pipes, with anecdotes.
rmueBVrLKcY.why: HN calls it a superb, funny and engaging talk, and links it often after Armstrong's death as one of his best.

rC4FCS-oMpg.summary: Rik Arends presents Makepad, a Rust UI framework, at RustNL 2023. The talk covers designing modern, GPU-fast UIs with Rust and includes live-coded demos of an IDE and a synthesizer.
rC4FCS-oMpg.why: HN commenters recommend it for the live-coded demos running at high frame rates, calling the performance impressive.

rQKis2Cfpeo.summary: A short clip of Steve Jobs arguing that the best people are self-managing and that professional managers who cannot do the work add little. He says leadership is about a shared vision.
rQKis2Cfpeo.why: Cited in threads on management, hiring and company culture for Jobs's views on self-managing people and small, self-policing core teams.

rkfAcWpOYAA.summary: A Berkeley Lab Distinguished Lecturer talk on building science, with an expert covering control layers, insulation and vapour barrier placement, and how buildings fail. The delivery is humorous.
rkfAcWpOYAA.why: HN commenters cite it as an authoritative, entertaining source on building science, such as insulation placement and why LEED point priorities miss the mark.

rsxCZAE8QNA.summary: Bill Dally of NVIDIA gives a Hot Chips 2023 keynote on the challenges of building hardware for deep learning. He traces how GPUs have been adapted for machine learning, especially training.
rsxCZAE8QNA.why: HN points to it for an insider view of why NVIDIA's AI gains came from design rather than process, and for data-movement power costs.

rwhUpu9MfZ0.summary: A long video essay by Skip Intro asking what vision of policing the kids' show PAW Patrol suggests. It mixes comedy with serious critique and features guest voices.
rwhUpu9MfZ0.why: Recommended as a funny but serious critique of the show's portrayal of authority and policing.

rCfPQLVzus4.summary: A detailed 40-minute explanation of the ultraviolet catastrophe, covering Rayleigh and Jeans' classical treatment of blackbody radiation and Planck's quantum hypothesis. It follows the Eisberg and Resnick textbook treatment.
rCfPQLVzus4.why: Recommended for a math-heavy but thorough treatment of the ultraviolet catastrophe and the history of the experiments.

rG_Eh0J_4_s.summary: Scott Manley explains rotating detonation engines, how they differ from pulsed detonation engines, and why thermodynamics predicts they beat traditional jet and rocket engines.
rG_Eh0J_4_s.why: Recommended as the introductory explainer whenever rotating detonation engines show up in the news.

rGgG-0lOJjk.summary: Yo-Yo Ma performs Bach's Cello Suite No. 1 in G Major at the BBC Proms in 2015. It is a full solo cello performance of the suite.
rGgG-0lOJjk.why: Offered as an entry point to Bach's cello suites, which HN commenters praise for evoking rich harmony from a single line.

rGqiswuJuQI.summary: Jaron Lanier delivers the 2018 Willy Brandt Lecture in Berlin on who civilization is for, covering data, AI, tech platforms and the economics of who benefits, followed by a Q&A with Germany's data protection commissioner Ulrich Kelber.
rGqiswuJuQI.why: HN cites it for Lanier's ideas on the circle of empathy and paying people whose data and work train AI.

rHKwIYsPXLg.summary: John Searle's Talk at Google on consciousness and artificial intelligence, hosted by Google's Singularity Network. He presents his philosophy of mind and Chinese room argument that computation is syntactic and cannot capture semantics.
rHKwIYsPXLg.why: Used as a source for Searle's own argument in Chinese room discussions, though some find nothing new in it.

rHdS_4GsKmg.summary: Clayton Christensen speaks at Google on where growth comes from, covering disruption, market-creating versus efficiency innovation, and jobs to be done. He also touches on measuring your life.
rHdS_4GsKmg.why: Referenced in threads about disruption and incumbents as a clear statement of his theories.

rQhzEnWCgHA.summary: Not Just Bikes explains how an electric bakfiets (Dutch cargo bike) replaced the family car after a move back to Canada, saving thousands of dollars. It shows how much it can carry, including kids and groceries.
rQhzEnWCgHA.why: HN commenters reach for it whenever cargo bikes come up as a practical car replacement for families.

rTawFwUvnLE.summary: Geoffrey Hinton gives an MIT talk on what is wrong with convolutional neural networks and introduces his capsules project. The description points to the capsule network papers.
rTawFwUvnLE.why: Recommended as Hinton's own explanation of capsule networks and his critique of pooling in CNNs.

rUg_ukBwsyo.summary: Jay Leno tours and drives a 1925 Doble E-20 steam car, once owned by Howard Hughes, covering how it starts up and runs. It includes a cutaway view of the engine.
rUg_ukBwsyo.why: Cited in steam car threads as a well-produced view of how a Doble works and how it solved startup in 1925.

rWRbTnE1PEM.summary: A 1997 interview with Jeff Bezos taped at a Special Libraries conference, where he explains why Amazon started with books and why the web made it possible. He calls it the Kitty Hawk stage of electronic commerce.
rWRbTnE1PEM.why: HN people share it as a precise, early statement of Amazon's pitch, useful for startup idea reasoning.

rWlk9HreE7U.summary: Milton Friedman lectures to physicians on the economics of medical care, arguing that government involvement raises costs and leads toward socialized medicine. He also discusses licensing and protecting patients from quacks.
rWlk9HreE7U.why: HN commenters recommend it for Friedman's argument that regulation and lobbying produce a less efficient, centrally planned healthcare system.

rpyBYuu-wJI.summary: ChefSteps shows how to make espresso-style coffee in a moka pot, with a bonus latte hack. It is a quick how-to aimed at home brewers.
rpyBYuu-wJI.why: HN commenters link it in moka pot threads as a practical guide whose tips, such as starting with hot water, improved their coffee.

ruNFcH-KibY.summary: Tikhon Jelvis's Compose Conference talk on using the Z3 SMT solver to analyze and verify programs, including checking invariants with bounded loops. He demonstrates verifying programs in a small language by compiling them to Z3.
ruNFcH-KibY.why: HN lists it among the practical entry points for learning Z3 and formal verification.

rzJqXd-1dEU.summary: Yuta, a Japanese YouTuber, tests how much simplified Chinese a Japanese person can read, working with a Mandarin speaker. The video shows where shared kanji help and where meanings differ.
rzJqXd-1dEU.why: HN uses it to answer whether Japanese speakers can read Chinese: they can guess a lot, but not reliably.

rcwngbUrZNg.summary: Joanna Rutkowska's 32C3 talk asks whether trustworthy client systems can be built on x86 hardware, and what realistically can be done about the challenges, such as Intel ME.
rcwngbUrZNg.why: Recommended in Intel ME threads as essential viewing on x86 trust and auxiliary processors.

rqOUgqsWvbw.summary: Aaron Boodman of Replicache asks why sync engines have not yet fixed web app complexity and what is missing for them to go mainstream. The talk lays out the ideas that led to the Zero sync engine.
rqOUgqsWvbw.why: Cited in sync-engine threads as the origin story for Zero and for hybrid local and remote queries.

rtd7UzLJHrU.summary: HDTVTest reviews the Apple Pro Display XDR using measurements and a side-by-side comparison with a Sony BVM-HX310 dual-layer LCD reference monitor. It examines how well the display handles HDR against a professional reference.
rtd7UzLJHrU.why: Cited both as a well-crafted monitor review and as evidence for the XDR's shortcomings versus reference displays, though some dispute its fairness.

r-TuGAHR78w.summary: Not Just Bikes tours Houten, a Dutch town designed around cycling, explaining how its layout makes most trips by bike safe and easy. It also promotes a book about the town.
r-TuGAHR78w.why: HN uses it as an example that car-free, leafy suburbs where kids can bike independently are possible.

rAZavOcEnLg.summary: A short demonstration of the MONIAC, Bill Phillips' hydro-mechanical economic computer, at the Reserve Bank of New Zealand museum. It shows how water flows model an economy's money flows.
rAZavOcEnLg.why: Brought up as a charming example of analog and liquid computers simulating a national economy.

rENyyRwxpHo.summary: A short Nature video on the discovery that our home supercluster is Laniakea, redefined by mapping the flow of galaxies rather than their density. It names the structure with a Hawaiian word meaning 'immeasurable heaven'.
rENyyRwxpHo.why: Linked as a quick visual intro to Laniakea and large-scale cosmic structure.

rE_M1n-ClOA.summary: Fully Charged rides a 100% battery-electric ferry across the 4 km strait between Helsingborg, Sweden and Helsingør, Denmark. The ferry crosses up to 46 times a day and charges for a few minutes at each side. The video shows the charging setup, including the robot arm that couples the charger.
rE_M1n-ClOA.why: HN commenters cite it as a concrete, working example of large-battery electric shipping with fast automated charging.

rEoc0YoALt0.summary: Steve Mould explains motion amplification and video magnification, techniques that find tiny changes in video invisible to the eye and exaggerate them. He covers the MIT research and industrial uses such as diagnosing vibrating machinery.
rEoc0YoALt0.why: Pointed to as an approachable layperson's explanation whenever video magnification or vibration visualization comes up.

rHFOwlMCdto.summary: A John Oliver Last Week Tonight segment on voting access in the US, covering how some states are making voting less equal. It is a comedic news commentary piece.
rHFOwlMCdto.why: Used in political threads as a reference on voter ID laws and their effects, and often rebutted or disputed in the replies.

rIAXIubSTkc.summary: Mentalist Derren Brown plays nine skilled English chess players, including four grandmasters, simultaneously on his TV show. The trick behind the apparent win is the point of the segment.
rIAXIubSTkc.why: HN cites it as a neat, simple trick of relaying moves between opponents, often in discussions of chess, AI or ludic fallacies.

rKnDgT73v8s.summary: Rob Pike's October 2009 Google Tech Talk introducing Go, a new experimental systems language designed for fast builds, concurrency and garbage collection. It covers the goals, syntax and type system.
rKnDgT73v8s.why: Used as the primary source for what Go's creators originally promised, such as fast compiles, systems-language framing, safety and generics.

rSAaiYKF0cs.summary: Daniel Radcliffe performs his party trick on The Graham Norton Show: singing Tom Lehrer's 'The Elements', the periodic table song, from memory. It is a two-minute talk-show clip.
rSAaiYKF0cs.why: Mentioned in Tom Lehrer threads as a charming example of Lehrer's song reaching a new audience.

rbsqaJwpu6A.summary: Demis Hassabis of DeepMind speaks at Google Zeitgeist, saying human-level AI is decades away but the debate should start now. He covers DeepMind's focus on game-playing agents.
rbsqaJwpu6A.why: HN cites it for the DeepMind CEO's early views on AI and its game-playing focus, in AlphaGo and OpenAI threads.

rf5o5liZxnA.summary: A 35-minute demonstration of NeXTSTEP Release 3 by Steve Jobs. It shows the object-oriented development environment and features such as dragging a live chart between apps.
rf5o5liZxnA.why: Cited as a primary source for what NeXTSTEP could do and how Jobs pitched rapid application development.

rh5J4vacG98.summary: A screencast tutorial on Specter, a Clojure library for navigating and transforming nested data structures declaratively, demonstrated in a REPL.
rh5J4vacG98.why: Pointed to as a short, clear demonstration of how Specter simplifies manipulating complex nested data.

ridS396W2BY.summary: A one-minute Volvo Trucks demo of the Collision Warning with Emergency Brake system on a fully loaded 40-ton tractor-trailer, avoiding a rear-end collision on a test track.
ridS396W2BY.why: Cited as a real-world example of automatic emergency braking already working on heavy trucks.

rnLWSC5p1XE.summary: Noam Chomsky gives a Talks at Google lecture covering his work on politics and language. It touches on his linguistic theory, including universal grammar, alongside his political criticism.
rnLWSC5p1XE.why: HN commenters point to it as an easy-to-grasp introduction to Chomsky's ideas on universal grammar and the language faculty.

rufnWLVQcKg.summary: A short 1966 propaganda interview clip in which Jeremiah Denton, a US prisoner of war in Vietnam, blinks the word TORTURE in Morse code. Naval Intelligence later decoded the message.
rufnWLVQcKg.why: Cited as the classic real-world use of Morse code to smuggle out a message under duress.

rvLFEh7V18A.summary: Karl Jobst investigates the retro video game bubble, examining who caused it, who profits, and how graders and auction houses like Wata Games and Heritage inflate prices. It runs almost an hour.
rvLFEh7V18A.why: HN points to it as investigative journalism backing the view that vintage game prices are inflated by wash trading and grading services.

rzXPyCY7jbs.summary: Slavoj Zizek speaks at an architecture congress in Pamplona about how toilet design in France, England and Germany reflects national ideology. The clip is about four minutes long.
rzXPyCY7jbs.why: Mostly posted as a joke in toilet-related threads, especially for the line about German hermeneutic stool inspection.

r-V_Z3bD_PA.summary: Dave Jones of EEVblog investigates why a 4K BenQ monitor switches itself off, tracing it to static discharge from an office chair. He uses an oscilloscope to examine the static impulses.
r-V_Z3bD_PA.why: Linked whenever someone reports a monitor blacking out from static electricity, as prior art on the same problem.

r38Epj6ldKU.summary: The Hated One argues that Apple tracks users and shares their data despite its privacy marketing, pointing to Apple's own privacy policy. It is a critical take on Apple as a corporation rather than a friend of privacy.
r38Epj6ldKU.why: Commenters post it as support for the view that Apple's privacy stance is mostly marketing.

r4wLXNydzeY.summary: A three-and-a-half-hour Lex Fridman interview with international relations scholar John Mearsheimer. He discusses war and power politics, covering Israel-Palestine, Russia-Ukraine, China, NATO, and the risk of a larger war.
r4wLXNydzeY.why: HN commenters cite it as a representative statement of Mearsheimer's realist views, such as anarchy among nation-states and Russia seeking early peace talks.

r6Kau7bO3Fw.summary: Rebecca Watson's video critiquing physicist Sabine Hossenfelder's earlier video on gender care for transgender minors, arguing it mishandled the evidence.
r6Kau7bO3Fw.why: HN users mainly link it as a rebuttal to Hossenfelder's trans-issues video when her credibility comes up.

r9-3K3rkPRE.summary: A New York Times Op-Doc by Laura Poitras profiling William Binney, a 32-year NSA veteran who helped design a secret program he says collects Americans' personal data.
r9-3K3rkPRE.why: Cited as a primary source for Binney's claims about NSA surveillance, including the FBI raid on his home.

rAYW9n8i-C4.summary: Veritasium shows an experiment from Prof. Dan Lathrop's lab with a spinning sphere of molten sodium, used to study how turbulent convection in Earth's core generates a magnetic field. It is a short demonstration of dynamo physics.
rAYW9n8i-C4.why: Cited as a visual example of dynamo flows and of the care needed when handling reactive liquid sodium.

rDqQcmVqAm4.summary: A roughly 72-minute interview with Steve Jobs, believed to come from the 1995 interviews made for the Triumph of the Nerds documentary. He reflects on Apple and the early computer industry.
rDqQcmVqAm4.why: Cited for first-person Jobs remarks, such as nobody knowing the market in the early days, and for dating the footage.

rDsTc2oWGSI.summary: A short Los Alamos National Laboratory safety video on how to use stairs, including handrail advice in a music-video style. It was posted as an example of government spending.
rDsTc2oWGSI.why: Cited as a joke or mild criticism of institutional safety culture at Los Alamos.

rERApU26PcA.summary: A short Star Trek TNG clip from 'Brothers' in which Data uses a lockout code with an unusually long, secret-sounding sequence.
rERApU26PcA.why: Used as a joke or a tongue-in-cheek reference in security and authentication threads.

rGfaJZAdfNE.summary: A 2015 CNBC Mad Money interview in which Jim Cramer gives Theranos CEO Elizabeth Holmes a platform to answer accusations about her company after critical press coverage. It captures her public persona at the height of the company's hype.
rGfaJZAdfNE.why: HN uses it as a primary source on Holmes's responses and, later, as evidence of her manner and voice.

rKaEhBjt1ls.summary: A Fully Charged episode on Ubitricity, a German company that turns ordinary street lamp posts into roughly 5 kW overnight EV charge points, with a locking cable and managed billing.
rKaEhBjt1ls.why: HN points to it as the real-world example for the garage orphan problem, meaning EV owners with no home charger.

rLDgQg6bq7o.summary: A short comedy video of the Turbo Encabulator, a piece of technobabble nonsense describing an imaginary machine in deadpan engineering language.
rLDgQg6bq7o.why: HN uses it as a joke reply to threads full of dense or impenetrable technical jargon.

rMz7JBRbmNo.summary: The poison goblet scene from The Princess Bride, in which Westley tricks Vizzini in a battle of wits. It is a famous example of nested reasoning.
rMz7JBRbmNo.why: Mostly used as a joke or parody reference, and occasionally as the canonical illustration of leveled, second-order thinking.

rVlhMGQgDkY.summary: Boston Dynamics unveils a new, smaller Atlas humanoid robot that is electrically powered and hydraulically actuated. It balances with body sensors and uses lidar and stereo vision to navigate and manipulate objects.
rVlhMGQgDkY.why: Used as a benchmark of robotics progress and a go-to example of impressive bipedal walking in AI and automation debates.

rY0WxgSXdEE.summary: The official remastered music video for Queen's Another One Bites the Dust from The Game (1980).
rY0WxgSXdEE.why: Not recommended; HN commenters invoke the title as a joke when a startup or product shuts down.

rYPMbLO4pAY.summary: A compilation of clips of diesel truck drivers rolling coal, blasting black exhaust smoke, at protesters. It is framed in a mocking political tone.
rYPMbLO4pAY.why: Used as a critical example of hostile, spiteful behavior and of the culture around coal rolling.

raNx9L4VH2k.summary: Robert Watson presents the Capsicum paper at USENIX Security 2010, describing practical capability-based sandboxing for UNIX. The paper won Best Student Paper.
raNx9L4VH2k.why: Referenced as the authoritative talk on Capsicum, including comparisons of how little code it takes to sandbox programs versus SELinux.

ramBFRt1Uzk.summary: Steven Pinker's TED talk charts the long decline of violence from biblical times to today, arguing that despite Iraq and Darfur we may be living in the most peaceful era of our species.
ramBFRt1Uzk.why: Cited as a counterpoint when threads claim the world is getting worse, and for Pinker's view that technology and trade create positive-sum interactions.

rbHxeOQA1Mc.summary: A video by expat YouTuber serpentza about animal-eating practices and hygiene in China, presented as showing what the country's authorities do not want seen.
rbHxeOQA1Mc.why: HN commenters link it during 2020 coronavirus threads as supposed evidence about exotic animal markets in China, rather than recommending it.

revk5r5vqxA.summary: The video argues that machine-learning-based aimbots, which read the screen and drive the controls externally, could make cheating in FPS games undetectable. It explains how conventional aimbots work, how the new approach differs, and speculates on possible detection.
revk5r5vqxA.why: HN uses it as a reference when discussing anti-cheat limits, particularly external hardware and AI cheats that bypass kernel-level protection.

rie-9AEhYdY.summary: Machine Learning Street Talk interviews Paul Lessard about Categorical Deep Learning, which uses category theory and monads to make neural network architectures more interpretable and composable. They also discuss neural networks' limits in reasoning and unbounded computation.
rie-9AEhYdY.why: Mostly cited in passing, e.g. regarding claims that transformers cannot do recursion and as an example of structured deep learning work.

rkuhWA9GdCo.summary: A four-minute 2017 clip of geopolitical analyst Peter Zeihan discussing a Russian land grab, in which he anticipated a Russian move on Ukraine.
rkuhWA9GdCo.why: Cited after the 2022 invasion as evidence Zeihan predicted the Ukraine war years earlier.

rld0KDcan_w.summary: A short George Carlin bit on the Earth and plastic, in which he suggests the planet may have let humans evolve just to make plastic. The upload is edited to be more safe for work.
rld0KDcan_w.why: Quoted as a joke in threads about plastic, climate and the meaning of life.

rmsIZUuBoQs.summary: A one-minute clip of Alan Kay giving his blunt critique of Linux and the Unix approach.
rmsIZUuBoQs.why: HN uses it as a quick citation of Alan Kay's dislike of Linux, in threads questioning whether the Unix way is the final word.

rnMsgxIIQEE.summary: In a short interview clip, physicist Murray Gell-Mann talks about working alongside Richard Feynman at Caltech. He describes how the two men clashed in personality and image despite similar brilliance.
rnMsgxIIQEE.why: HN commenters cite it for Gell-Mann's candid and not always flattering view of Feynman's showmanship and character.

rpkoCZ4vBSI.summary: Clayton Christensen explains his theory of disruptive innovation at Oxford's Said Business School, using examples from steel, Toyota, Sony, Walmart and Godrej. He applies the theory to why some economies stagnate and others grow.
rpkoCZ4vBSI.why: HN uses it as a reference for disruption theory when explaining why incumbents like VW or BlackBerry decline.

rrBxZGWCdgs.summary: Satirist Ami Horowitz interviews people at UC Berkeley and in Harlem about whether voter ID laws suppress the black vote. It is a short Fox News segment contrasting responses from white liberals with those from black residents.
rrBxZGWCdgs.why: Cited in political threads as a partisan example of how liberals view minority voters, with some commenters treating it as funny.

rsL6mKxtOlQ.summary: A three-minute clip of George Carlin's bit on the American dream, arguing that the owners of the country do not want an educated population capable of critical thinking.
rsL6mKxtOlQ.why: Quoted in threads about education, inequality and critical thinking as a cynical take on who benefits from the system.

rthHSISkM7A.summary: A clip from the 1985 comedy Real Genius in which a laser ignites a giant container of popcorn inside a house.
rthHSISkM7A.why: Not recommended; commenters use it as a joke reference in threads about military lasers and similar technology.

rvQ9DjJNal0.summary: A vlog in which Tucker Gott flies a paramotor to a McDonald's for lunch, showing everyday powered paraglider flying.
rvQ9DjJNal0.why: Used as a vivid example of personal flight that needs no airport, often in threads on drones and aviation regulation.

rvYuoWyk8iU.summary: A short clip from the British sitcom Yes Minister in which Sir Humphrey cynically explains to Jim Hacker why European nations joined the common market.
rvYuoWyk8iU.why: HN quotes it in threads about the EU as a satirical explanation of how Brussels bureaucracy came about.

rweblFwt-BM.summary: A short clip in which Thomas Sowell argues that demand for intellectuals is manufactured by intellectuals, using global warming predictions as an example. It is an excerpt from a longer talk on his book Intellectuals and Society.
rweblFwt-BM.why: Mostly debated or criticized; one commenter found his points fair, while others questioned his climate views.

rwgpTDluufY.summary: Louis Rossmann criticizes Apple's independent repair provider program as a PR move with invasive contract terms. He argues it does little for independent shops or customers.
rwgpTDluufY.why: Cited in right-to-repair threads as a repair-shop view of why Apple's program is impractical.

rwvIGNXY21Y.summary: Mathematician singingbanana shows how he flipped ten heads in a row, with the full uncut video and answers to viewers' questions. The point is that unlikely events happen given enough attempts.
rwvIGNXY21Y.why: Used as a reference for the perseverance behind improbable streaks and selective reporting of best runs.

rxPa9A-k2xY.summary: A short clip shows the horizontal stabilizer jackscrew of a Boeing 737NG cycling through its motion. It illustrates how pitch trim is physically adjusted.
rxPa9A-k2xY.why: HN used it during 737 Max crash discussions to show how the stabilizer trim works and why manual trimming takes time.

ryFB6mvy4uE.summary: Jason Calacanis interviews Peter Thiel at LAUNCH Festival 2015 about contrarian thinking, investing, and building companies such as PayPal, Palantir and Facebook.
ryFB6mvy4uE.why: HN mostly cites it for specific anecdotes, such as Thiel's early Facebook investment and how he thinks about the future, not as a general recommendation.
